results.title: AI Usability Issue Detector in Figma Design | Figma
results.content:
Figma's agent can surface potential problem areas in your UI—places where users might get confused, miss important actions, or encounter accessibility barriers. By analyzing your layout, component usage, and content structure, it flags areas that could cause friction. Think of it as a design-focused review that catches issues before they become user complaints or failed accessibility audits.

AI usability detection is best for catching common, pattern-based issues—contrast problems, missing labels, unclear layouts. It may not catch context-dependent problems that require understanding user intent, business logic, or edge cases. Figma's agent provides a helpful first pass, but it works best when combined with real user testing and expert accessibility review for critical flows. [...] Watch now

## FAQ

Figma's agent can flag common usability concerns like insufficient color contrast, small touch targets, unclear visual hierarchy, confusing navigation patterns, and missing labels or alt text. It reviews your actual design context—components, layout, and structure—to surface issues that might cause friction for real users. While it catches many common problems, it works best alongside human review for nuanced accessibility needs.

results.title: Figma’s Design Agent, Now With Custom Tools and Greater Context | Figma Blog
results.content:
## Build your own tools

###### Customer snapshot: Edward Chechique

Product designer Edward Chechique’s generative plugins import HTML to the canvas, create dashboard layouts, and visualize data. Before, building them was a frustrating process. “I would need to ask a favor from a developer who may not have time to help me,” says Edward. “Later, AI tools made it possible, but I still had to switch between different tools and workflows. Now with the agent in Figma, it’s much faster and easier because I can just ask for what I want directly. I’ve gone from zero possibilities to great possibilities.”
